result:
The proposed solution rests on a wrong weighting, so I reject it.

For two uniform random points, the line through them has density proportional to the chord length cubed, not squared. Writing the points as positions t₁, t₂ along a line L, the area element is dx dy = |t₁−t₂| dt₁ dt₂ dL. Integrating over positions on a chord of length l gives ∫∫|t₁−t₂| dt₁ dt₂ = l³/3. So the correct weight is l³ dL.

This also shows up in the stated total. By Crofton's formula, ∫ l³ dL = 3A² over all lines hitting a convex region of area A. For a unit-side hexagon, A = 3√3/2, so this equals 81/4. The solution's "22/3" does not match this, and ∫ l² dL would not give a clean value of that form anyway.

Since the method uses the wrong measure, the resulting closed form 27(ln 3 + 2√3 − 4)/22 ≈ 0.6906 has no justification. I did not recompute the correct value.

VERDICT: REJECT
